# Lite requirements document — Repository changelog

A changelog for this repository: a `CHANGELOG.md` at the root that records each release's
user-facing changes, newest first, and one README sentence pointing to it. It matters
because the repository keeps no record of what changed between releases, so a reader
can't tell what a new version changes for them.

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**
A reader of this repository has no way to see what changed from one version to the next.
There is no changelog, no git tag and no GitHub release, so the only record is the commit
history, which mixes kit test runs with changes a reader would care about. When a new
version appears, the reader has to read commits to work out what it changes for them.

**Who is affected?**
- **Readers of the repository:** people looking at kit-scratch as a worked example of what
  the ai-delivery kit (the Claude Code skills this repository exercises) produces. They
  need to see what each version contains without reading the commit history.
  **[ASSUMPTION]** Neither request names the reader; this is inferred from the README,
  which describes the repository as a worked example.
- **The maintainer, Max Adamsky:** asked for both changes, and adds entries as versions
  are released.

**What exists today?**
- No `CHANGELOG.md`, no git tags and no GitHub releases (checked 2026-09-29).
- `pyproject.toml` declares the project `kit-scratch-text-tools` at version `0.1.0`. It was
  first committed on 2026-09-17.
- `README.md` is three short paragraphs. The last one links to the pull request checklist
  in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Nothing in it mentions a changelog.
- The repository holds `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/decisions.md`,
  `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and the kit's own `.ai-delivery/` folder. It has no Python
  modules and no tests.

**How success is judged:**
A reader who starts from the README reaches the changelog in one step, and can tell from
it what version `0.1.0` contains without opening the commit history.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**
- `CHANGELOG.md` at the repository root, listing each release's user-facing changes,
  newest first, starting with one entry for version `0.1.0`.
- One sentence in `README.md` linking to it, together with the refreshed kit setup record
  that editing `README.md` requires.

**Out of Scope:**
- Rebuilding past entries from the commit history. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 2]**
- Automated changelog generation, including tools that build it from commit messages.
- Creating git tags or GitHub releases.
- A rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md` requiring contributors to update the changelog.
  **[ASSUMPTION — open question 4]**
- Changing the version number in `pyproject.toml`.
- Any change to the kit.

---

## 3. Units of Work

- **Unit 1 (Urgent): Record version 0.1.0 in a changelog at the repository root.** A
  reader can see, in one file, what version `0.1.0` of this repository contains, and later
  versions will be added above it. This unit touches only `CHANGELOG.md`, a new file.
- **Unit 2 (High): Link the changelog from the README.** A reader who starts from the
  README, the first thing anyone sees on the repository page, reaches the changelog in one
  step. This unit touches only `README.md` and the kit's setup record. Its link target is
  fixed as `CHANGELOG.md` at the repository root, so both units can be built at the same
  time.

**Happy path:** Reader opens the repository → reads the README → follows the changelog
link → sees the newest version first → reads what it changed for them → Done

---

## 4. Requirements

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | `CHANGELOG.md` at the repository root records the repository's releases. | Urgent | The file exists at the root. It opens with a title and one or two sentences saying what it records, that the newest version comes first, and what counts as a release. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 1]** A release is a new `version` value in `pyproject.toml`. |
| FR-002 | Each release has its own section, newest first. | High | Each release is one second-level heading holding the version number and its release date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form. Headings appear in descending version order, so a new release goes directly under the Unreleased section (FR-004). |
| FR-003 | The first entry records version `0.1.0`. | High | A `0.1.0` section lists what a reader of the repository gets in that version: the README describing what the repository is for, the pull request checklist in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the Python project declaration with its development toolchain. Each item is one plain sentence a reader can act on, with no commit hashes and no kit test-run detail. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 6]** The date is 2026-09-17, the day `pyproject.toml` declaring `0.1.0` was committed. |
| FR-004 | An Unreleased section sits above the newest release. | Medium | The first section after the introduction is headed Unreleased. It holds changes that have landed but not yet been released, and is empty when there are none. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 2]** |
| FR-005 | Entries follow the "Keep a Changelog" 1.1.0 layout. | Medium | Within each release, changes are grouped under that layout's headings (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security), and only headings with at least one entry appear. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 3]** |
| FR-006 | `README.md` links to the changelog. | High | `README.md` gains one sentence containing a relative link to `CHANGELOG.md`, and the link opens the file on GitHub. **[ASSUMPTION — open question 5]** The sentence goes after the existing pull request checklist sentence at the end of the README. No other line of `README.md` changes. |
| FR-007 | The kit's setup check still passes after the README changes. | Medium | Once the change lands, the kit's setup check reports FRESH, not STALE. The refreshed setup record, `.ai-delivery/stack-fingerprint`, lands in the same change as the README sentence. That file stores a hash of `README.md`, so any README edit makes the check report STALE until setup re-runs. This is Medium rather than High because a setup re-run clears it at any time. |

**Design-system components:** none. The work is not UI-facing.

**Key constraints:**
- **The setup record.** Editing `README.md` makes the kit's setup check report STALE, and
  every kit skill that checks setup then stops until setup re-runs. Adding `CHANGELOG.md`
  should not have this effect: the setup record tracks `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  but not `CHANGELOG.md` (checked against `.ai-delivery/stack-fingerprint`, 2026-09-29).
- **Which branch readers see.** GitHub shows readers the `main` branch. This branch,
  `live-proof-3.0.1`, is 24 commits ahead of `main`, so neither file reaches readers until
  this work merges to `main`. How that happens is outside this feature's scope.
- **Tooling and effort.** No new tooling and no automation. The work is two small
  documentation edits. The repository is the kit's test bed, so changes stay small and
  ordinary.

## Open Questions

Max Adamsky owns every question below. Each one carries a working answer, marked
**[ASSUMPTION]** where it is used above. Max Adamsky accepted all six working answers on
2026-09-29 by approving this document as written, so each question is closed on its
working answer.

- [x] **1. What counts as a release?** The repository has no git tags, so nothing else
  marks one. Assumed: a release is a new `version` value in `pyproject.toml`, and `0.1.0`
  is the first and only release so far. Affects FR-001.
- [x] **2. What does the changelog start with?** Assumed: one `0.1.0` entry summarising
  what the repository offers today, with an empty Unreleased section above it, rather than
  entries rebuilt from the 33 commits of history. Affects FR-003 and FR-004.
- [x] **3. Which format?** Assumed: the "Keep a Changelog" 1.1.0 layout, a widely used
  convention with a fixed set of change headings. The alternative is a plainer list per
  version. Affects FR-005.
- [x] **4. Who keeps the changelog current, and how?** Assumed: the maintainer adds
  entries at each release, and no contributor rule is added to `CONTRIBUTING.md` in this
  feature. Affects scope.
- [x] **5. Where does the README link go?** Assumed: one sentence after the existing pull
  request checklist sentence at the end of the README. Affects FR-006.
- [x] **6. What date does `0.1.0` carry?** No tag or release records one. Assumed:
  2026-09-17, the day `pyproject.toml` declaring `0.1.0` was committed. Affects FR-003.

No question in this document remains open.
